data.one_liner: Behavior-first headless UI components for Flutter that separate state from presentation.
data.what_it_does: Provides headless, unstyled UI widgets with built-in accessibility, semantics, and observable states like hover, focus, and drag. Allows developers to build custom interfaces with complete design control.
use_when: You need complete design control over UI components without pre-styled Material or Cupertino baggage.
You need robust accessibility semantics and observable interaction states for custom widgets.
You want standard behaviors like comboboxes, menus, dialogs, and sliders with custom styling.
avoid_when: You want a ready-to-use UI kit with out-of-the-box visual styling like Material Design.
You do not need headless widgets and prefer standard pre-styled components.
strengths: Complete separation of state and presentation for total design control.
Built-in accessibility semantics and screen reader support.
Rich set of supported components including menus, dialogs, sliders, and text fields.
weaknesses: Requires writing all visual styling and builders manually from scratch.
Does not provide its own design system or visual themes.
data.minimal_example:
NakedButton(
  onPressed: () => print('Clicked'),
  builder: (context, state, child) => Container(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.all(12),
    color: state.when(
      pressed: Colors.blue.shade900,
      hovered: Colors.blue.shade700,
      focused: Colors.blue.shade600,
      orElse: Colors.blue,
    ),
    child: const Text('Click Me', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.white)),
  ),
)
